sources.outlet: University of Minnesota Center for Urban & Regional Affairs (CURA)
sources.quote: Due to the older properties in Minnesota and Iowa, over half of properties in both states may never have had a restrictive use clause or these clauses have expired as of June 30, 2020.
sources.searcher_note: Same measure (no live restrictive-use clause), same USDA RD Active Projects dataset (2020-07-17 pull), Iowa named; window is June 2020 and counts properties, not pre-1981 units. Also: 44% of units in MN/IA/WI had lost or never had the clause. Page tagged FIRP 2020-2021; no date printed. No Missouri.

sources.quote: Several Midwestern states lost over 10% of their USDA Section 515 housing, including Nebraska, North Dakota, Michigan, South Dakota, Wisconsin, Indiana, and Iowa.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Summarizes HAC brief: 621 properties / 14,928 units left Section 515 (June 2021 to March 2025/2026; page gives both). Measures units already lost, not units without a live clause.

sources.quote: about 60 percent of properties with maturing mortgages exited the program between 2014 through 2017.
sources.searcher_note: GAO-18-285: over 90% of RHS properties/units (407,000 units) could exit 2028-2050; tenants may lose rental assistance when mortgages mature. National pattern, no restrictive-clause count.

sources.quote: Mortgages financed before December 21, 1979 can be prepaid only after the owner requests RD permission, rejects incentives to stay in the program, and sometimes offers the property to nonprofit or public entities.
sources.searcher_note: Mechanism: pre-1979 loans still face prepayment restrictions while the loan is outstanding; 1979-89 loans had 15- or 20-year use restrictions. Bears on the lead's caveat that the loan can still bind the project.

sources.outlet: Georgia Tech News Center (republished from The Conversation)
sources.quote: The owners of these rental properties no longer have to keep rents affordable once they have paid off their loans.
sources.searcher_note: Recent explainer by Brian Y. An: 90% of remaining Section 515 homes mature by 2045; rental assistance can be lost at payoff. No state figures.

notes: Section 515 is widely covered as a pattern (maturing mortgages, expired use restrictions, lost rental assistance). The closest match is CURA's Minnesota/Iowa/Wisconsin analysis, which measures the same thing (properties with no live restrictive-use clause) from the same USDA dataset but as of June 2020, by property, not limited to projects opened by 1980. No source found gives the 56,159-unit or 35,324-rental-assistance figures, or Missouri 32%. No Missouri-specific coverage found. No source disagreeing on direction found.
